description: Career-mode roles and actions. Attribute effects are bounded by 0 and 100. Thresholds are game rules, not a statement of official UK appointment procedures.

party_loyalist.label: Party loyalist
party_loyalist.description: Earn trust by being reliable and helping the party deliver.

campaigner.label: Constituency campaigner
campaigner.description: Focus on local service, public recognition and your seat.

rebel.label: Independent-minded rebel
rebel.description: Build a profile by challenging the party line, at a cost to party trust.

mp.label: Backbench MP
mp.description: Represent your constituency, scrutinise the government, make speeches and build a record in Parliament.

actions.label: Hold a constituency surgery
actions.description: Meet residents and resolve local casework. Reliable constituency service builds trust over time.

actions.label: Ask a probing parliamentary question
actions.description: Put a minister under scrutiny and develop a reputation for understanding policy.

actions.label: Run a local campaign
actions.description: Organise volunteers around an issue important to your seat.

actions.label: Prepare evidence for a committee
actions.description: Study a policy area and build relationships with other MPs.

actions.label: Give a media interview
actions.description: Raise your public profile, but your words may annoy party colleagues.

actions.label: Defy the party whip
actions.description: Vote against the party on a matter of principle. Some voters approve, but promotion becomes harder.

actions.label: Press a minister at Question Time
actions.description: Prepare a focused oral question and follow up when the minister's answer is vague. Good scrutiny builds influence, but government colleagues may resent repeated attacks.

actions.label: Sponsor a Private Member's Bill
actions.description: Draft a small legislative proposal and seek cross-party backing. It can raise your profile even if it does not become law; the action is not a guarantee of passage.

actions.label: Join a cross-party policy group
actions.description: Work with MPs from other parties on a focused issue, building expertise and relationships outside your own party.

actions.label: Write to a minister about a constituency problem
actions.description: Use a constituent's case to press the relevant department for action. It is less visible than a media campaign but can demonstrate practical representation.

pps.label: Parliamentary Private Secretary
pps.description: Act as a link between a minister and MPs, listen to backbench concerns and help understand parliamentary arithmetic. This is a junior political appointment, not a ministerial office.

actions.label: Brief the minister on backbench concerns
actions.description: Give the minister early warning of dissatisfaction and suggest a compromise.

actions.label: Organise support for a government bill
actions.description: Check how colleagues intend to vote and relay concerns to the whips.

actions.label: Draft a practical policy memo
actions.description: Turn a minister's broad idea into a concise set of options.

actions.label: Protect time for constituency work
actions.description: Show that a Westminster appointment has not made you forget your local responsibilities.

committee_chair.label: Select Committee Chair
committee_chair.description: Lead evidence sessions and scrutinise departmental decisions. A report can shape debate, but ministers do not automatically have to accept it.

actions.label: Launch a major inquiry
actions.description: Focus the committee on a policy failure or a long-term challenge.

actions.label: Call senior witnesses
actions.description: Gather evidence from officials, experts and affected groups.

actions.label: Publish a cross-party report
actions.description: Build consensus around practical recommendations.

actions.label: Confront a minister over poor delivery
actions.description: Demand answers publicly. It may raise your profile but close doors in government.

junior_minister.label: Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State
junior_minister.description: Take responsibility for a defined policy area, answer questions and help turn the department's plans into delivery.

actions.label: Set a departmental delivery plan
actions.description: Agree a small number of measurable goals with officials.

actions.label: Meet frontline workers and stakeholders
actions.description: Hear what is working and what is failing before changing policy.

actions.label: Prepare for parliamentary questions
actions.description: Answer difficult questions accurately and avoid an avoidable political row.

actions.label: Take ownership of a delivery problem
actions.description: Fix the issue rather than blaming officials. It costs political capital but builds credibility.

minister_of_state.label: Minister of State
minister_of_state.description: Lead a substantial part of a department, negotiate with colleagues and show that policies are producing results.

actions.label: Roll out a flagship programme
actions.description: Deliver a visible policy improvement, while accepting responsibility for the outcome.

actions.label: Negotiate with the Treasury
actions.description: Make the case for funding while showing how the programme will be paid for.

actions.label: Defend the policy in the Commons
actions.description: Answer criticism and explain the trade-offs honestly.

actions.label: Resolve a department-officials dispute
actions.description: Find a workable settlement instead of allowing delivery to stall.

secretary_state.label: Secretary of State
secretary_state.description: Lead an entire department, set priorities, negotiate its budget and defend its performance in Parliament and the media.

actions.label: Drive a major departmental reform
actions.description: Spend political capital on a long-term change that could become your signature achievement.

actions.label: Broker a Cabinet agreement
actions.description: Secure support from other departments for a shared priority.

actions.label: Lead a departmental crisis response
actions.description: Show judgement under pressure. A good response builds integrity; a poor one will be remembered.

actions.label: Make a case for the next spending review
actions.description: Trade lower-priority demands for funding that will actually improve delivery.

chancellor.label: Chancellor of the Exchequer
chancellor.description: Set fiscal strategy, negotiate departmental settlements and balance growth, public services, debt and market confidence.

actions.label: Prepare a credible Budget
actions.description: Build a fiscally coherent package and explain its trade-offs to Parliament.

actions.label: Meet investors and the OBR
actions.description: Explain the fiscal plan, acknowledge risks and avoid promising impossible savings.

actions.label: Back a long-term growth plan
actions.description: Prioritise skills, investment and productivity rather than a short-lived headline.

actions.label: Negotiate a tough departmental settlement
actions.description: Protect the fiscal rules but risk tension with Cabinet colleagues.

prime_minister.label: Prime Minister
prime_minister.description: Set the national agenda, chair Cabinet, handle crises, hold your party together and remain able to command the confidence of the House of Commons.

actions.label: Reshape the Cabinet
actions.description: Reward delivery, resolve a dispute or remove a minister who has lost your confidence.

actions.label: Prepare for Prime Minister's Questions
actions.description: Anticipate the opposition's attack and offer a defensible answer.

actions.label: Chair a national crisis meeting
actions.description: Coordinate departments, communicate clearly and accept accountability.

actions.label: Launch a constituency and national campaign
actions.description: Rebuild confidence in your leadership and connect national promises to voters' lives.
